correctness.rationale: Prime-order Fourier minors bound the two transformed zero counts by s-1. Any hypothetical support sum <=13 creates s+1 prescribed transform zeros on an original support of size s, so a cyclotomic (s+1)-by-s coefficient matrix would lose rank. Specializing omega to 105 mod the prime 1009, every one of 149793 such matrices has full column rank by complete exact elimination, as independently reproduced in integer arithmetic. A nonzero specialized minor implies a nonzero complex cyclotomic minor. The exact delta_0-delta_1 witness has supports (2,6,6). Only finite-dimensional and explicitly enumerated configurations are asserted.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A lower bound of 44 on the sum in eight bases does not yield 14 on a chosen three: bounding the other five supports above by 7 only yields 44-35=9. Theorem 8 concerns saturating the complete-set bound. Even the known prohibition of the symmetric 4+4+4 pattern does not exclude all 4+4+5 or 3+5+5 cases needed for the sharp 14 threshold.

value.rationale: The exact minimum for three natural mutually unbiased harmonic bases is a motivated support-uncertainty invariant singled out in the 2022 source as a future direction. It strengthens the general pairwise 12 bound to sharp 14 and excludes asymmetric sum-13 zero configurations, not determined by known pairwise or complete-eight-family results. The exact certificate makes this natural small-prime threshold reproducible without assuming probabilistic numerical evidence.
